sample_unit: patients (pilot neuroimaging dataset, bootstrapped into simulated datasets of 66-68)

links.outcome: Change in ML feature importance across simulated datasets with different cohort proportions
links.effect: Differing proportions of anosmic and non-anosmic cohorts in bootstrapped datasets (matched, 73% non-anosmic, 76% anosmic) altered key feature importance and even the presence or absence of features.
links.quote: We found that the differing proportions of the same cohorts represented in each hypothetical dataset altered not only the relative importance of key features distinguishing between them but even the presence or absence of such features.

unlisted_practices: Using bootstrap resampling to simulate disproportionate datasets as an 'AI ethics' experiment
Establishing a regional (South East Asian) neuroimaging repository to redress global data imbalance
Ethical framework for including migrant workers in neuroimaging repositories

screen.reason: The paper includes an empirical simulation experiment testing how demographic/cohort imbalances in neuroimaging datasets affect ML feature selection and bias.
